title: Backcast from Closed AI-Orchestrated Attack: What Indicators Would Have Provided Early Warning?

original_idea.body:
# Backcast from Closed AI-Orchestrated Attack: What Indicators Would Have Provided Early Warning?

**Problem:** The November 2025 Anthropic case documented the first AI-orchestrated state-sponsored cyberattack (80-90% automation, 30 targets). Working backward: what evaluation results, if they had existed beforehand, would have provided actionable warning that this capability level had been reached?

**Direction:** Reconstruct the capability profile implied by the attack description (reconnaissance, credential harvesting, lateral movement, data extraction — all mostly automated). Map these capabilities to existing benchmark task types. Identify which benchmark combination would have predicted 80%+ automation capability. Determine whether those benchmarks existed and what their scores were at the time of the attack.

**Why it matters:** If existing benchmarks would have predicted this capability level, the evaluation ecosystem is working but the warning was ignored. If no existing benchmark would have predicted it, there is a fundamental evaluation blind spot that requires new benchmark development.

**Relevant context:** Anthropic November 2025 report on AI-orchestrated espionage (anthropic.com/news/disrupting-AI-espionage). Anthropic's China attack involved 30 global targets with 80-90% automation. AISI 22/32 steps was the best published performance at a similar time. OCCULT was contemporaneous. This is a direct forensic analysis of a real incident.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Retrospective analysis is valuable but has unclear direct pathway to reducing catastrophic risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires access to LLM APIs, security infrastructure, and sophisticated evaluation design. Likely beyond beginner capability.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Analysis of existing capabilities to infer missing ones; requires clear methodology but bounded scope.
